## Why the review looks like this
The half‑precision candidate runs fastest on the hardware and uses the least power so it is the natural first build to test.  
The success comparisons still show wide overlapping intervals and too few trials so a clear decision cannot yet be made.  
A simple input sanity check catches the deliberately miscalibrated builds before any further analysis leading to their rejection.  
In held‑out trials the AI judge found most problematic cases while raising only a small number of false alerts indicating it can be trusted to flag issues.  

## Questions to resolve before deployment
- Does the half‑precision candidate achieve a success rate that is clearly better than the reference when more trials are run?  
- Do the stress tests on unseen configurations show any deviation beyond the tolerance threshold after additional runs?  
- Can the simple input check be strengthened to catch any future miscalibration without relying on offline audits?  
- Does the AI judge maintain low false alarm rates when evaluated on newer data sets from different lighting conditions?  
- Is the power consumption of the half‑precision build within the expected budget for long missions?
